name: Pressure washing business
blurb: Clean driveways, decks, walls and roofs with a pressure washer, paid per job
title: Pressure Washing Business: How It Works, Costs and Risks
description: How a pressure washing or power washing business makes money, the kit and runoff rules involved, who it suits, the risks and how to test it first.
h1: How to start a pressure washing business
answer: A pressure washing (or power washing) business cleans driveways, patios, decks, fences, building walls and sometimes roofs, and charges per job or per area. A first machine and kit can start small, and jobs are quick to show off with before-and-after photos. The catches are seasonality, the risk of damaging surfaces, and rules about where dirty wash water can go.

sections.h: How a pressure washing business makes money
body: Most jobs are priced per job or per square foot or metre, with add-ons such as sealing a deck, cleaning gutters or treating stains. Homeowners book one-off cleans; shops, restaurants and property managers can become repeat clients for storefronts, car parks and bin areas.
Margin goes to fuel, water, cleaning chemicals, equipment wear, insurance and travel. A bigger machine finishes jobs faster, which matters because your time on site is what limits income.

ul: A pressure washer suited to the work, plus surface cleaners, hoses, nozzles and protective gear. Many operators start with a smaller unit and rent bigger ones for the occasional large job.
A vehicle or trailer to carry the kit, and access to water at each site.
Knowledge of which surfaces need low pressure or soft washing, so you do not etch wood, strip paint or force water behind siding.
Liability insurance, since damage to property or a passer-by is a real risk.

Local paperwork: rules differ by country and city. Many places restrict letting dirty wash water or chemicals run into storm drains; check with your city or environmental regulator, and ask about any business licence you need.

sections.h: Who it suits (and who it doesn't)

head: Suits
Not for
rows: People who like outdoor, physical work
Anyone who wants steady income all year without a plan for the off-season
Someone handy with engines and equipment
People not comfortable on ladders or roofs
Good self-promoters who can use photos
Places where water use or runoff rules make jobs impractical

ul: Surface damage: too much pressure can scar wood, damage mortar or strip paint, and the client will expect you to pay for it.
Seasonality: cold or wet months slow bookings in many climates, so cash from busy months has to last.
Water and chemical rules: runoff into storm drains can lead to fines in some places; containment or recovery may be required.
Injury: high-pressure water can cause serious injuries, and ladder or roof work adds fall risk.
Low entry cost means competitors can undercut you; quality, reliability and reviews are the defence.

sections.h: How to test it cheaply first

ol: Check maps and local listings for pressure washing services nearby and note what they offer.
Rent or borrow a machine and clean your own driveway or a friend's patio to learn the technique.
Do three paid jobs for neighbours at a fair price and time each one, including set-up and clean-up.
Take before-and-after photos and post one offer in a local group; count real enquiries over two weeks.
Ask your local authority what applies to wash water before you buy anything.
Register the business, get liability insurance and confirm local runoff rules.
Buy a machine sized for residential driveways and patios first, not the biggest rig.
Set a price list with a minimum charge and a written note on what you will not guarantee, such as old stains.
Build a photo portfolio and ask every client for a review.
Approach a few shops or property managers about regular storefront or car park cleans to smooth out the seasons.

faq.q: What is the difference between pressure washing and power washing?
faq.a: The terms are often used for the same service. Some operators use power washing to mean heated water, which helps with grease and oil, but customers usually search for either phrase.
Soft washing uses low pressure with cleaning solutions to clean roofs, render and painted surfaces that high pressure could damage. Learn it before taking on roofs and delicate exteriors.

faq.q: Can I do pressure washing as a side hustle?
faq.a: Yes, many people start on weekends because jobs are short and clients are often home. Plan for weather cancellations and for slow months in winter.
